name: Canada
summary: Three national operators (Rogers, Bell, TELUS — Bell and TELUS share a RAN) plus Vidéotron/Freedom (Quebecor), which took over Freedom Mobile's network and spectrum as the Rogers–Shaw merger remedy in April 2023, and regional carriers (Eastlink, SaskTel, TbayTel, Xplore). All licences are regional (ISED Tier 1–5 service areas), so holdings are shown as population-weighted national averages.

operators.name: Rogers
operators.notes: Acquired Shaw Communications on 3 Apr 2023 (Shaw's own spectrum incl. the AWS-1 licences it had sold to Rogers earlier stayed with Rogers; Freedom Mobile was divested to Vidéotron). Also holds former Mobilicity (DAVE Wireless) AWS-1 licences (2015).

operators.name: Bell
operators.notes: Includes Bell MTS (Manitoba Telecom Services, acquired 2017) and Northwestel. Shares its RAN with TELUS nationally; site-data uploads for the shared network are therefore not a guide to each partner's licences.

operators.name: TELUS
operators.notes: Reports licensed gross national mobile spectrum holdings averaging 270 MHz (2025 annual report). Includes former Public Mobile PCS-G licences (2013).

operators.name: Vidéotron / Freedom
operators.notes: Bought Freedom Mobile (incl. all Freedom/Wind spectrum licences) from Shaw/Rogers as the Rogers–Shaw merger remedy, closed 3 Apr 2023; ISED site data (Sep 2026) lists the former Freedom 600 MHz, 700 MHz and AWS-3 licences under Vidéotron ltée. The Freedom licences carry a 10-year transfer restriction imposed by ISED.

operators.name: Xplore
operators.notes: Formerly Xplornet; rural fixed-wireless and satellite ISP.

operators.name: Cogeco
operators.notes: Cable operator; won 3500 MHz licences in 2021 and 2500 MHz residual licences in 2018.

operators.name: Elite GP
operators.notes: Won 3800 MHz licences in 2023; affiliation not checked.

notes: Licensing is regional: auctioned bands use ISED Tier 2 (14 areas: 600, 700, AWS-3, AWS-1 B/C), Tier 3 (59: 2500, AWS-1 A/D/E/F), Tier 4 (172: 3500, 3800) or Tier 5 (mmWave) service areas. Holdings are pop-weighted national averages computed here from ISED's published auction results (per-licence tables and xlsx files) using the census populations in those files (2006, 2011 or 2016). They are approximations: later transfers are applied only where known (see operator notes) and populations differ by census year.

Ownership changes applied to auction results: Shaw → Rogers (3 Apr 2023); Freedom Mobile/Wind → Vidéotron (3 Apr 2023, merger remedy; ISED site data Sep 2026 confirms Vidéotron ltée as licensee of the former Freedom 600/700/AWS-3 licences); Mobilicity (DAVE Wireless) → Rogers (2015); Shaw AWS-1 → Rogers (2013–15); MTS → Bell (2017); Public Mobile → TELUS (2013); Xplornet → Xplore; Bragg = Eastlink.

Cross-checks: Rogers' 2025 annual report (600: 20–40 MHz; 700: 24 MHz; 850: 25 MHz; 2500: 40 MHz FDD; 3500: 60–80 MHz in large centres; 3500+3800: 100 MHz combined) matches the computed averages. TELUS reports 270 MHz gross national average; the computed TELUS total here (incl. PCS estimate, excl. AWS-4/WCS) is ~250 MHz.

3800 MHz: the 3500+3800 cross-band cap of 100 MHz per licensee per Tier 4 area applies for five years from 3800 licence issuance. 3900–3980 MHz and parts of 26/28/38 GHz are reserved for non-competitive local licensing (NCLL).
Band edges: licences within a band are assigned per service area, so block positions differ between areas; no national block positions are drawn.
missing: PCS 1900: Bell and TELUS amounts are estimates (combined ≈2×34 MHz remainder after Rogers and minor licensees); no source gives their pop-weighted PCS holdings. from background knowledge / derivation, not source-verified.
850 MHz B-block split between Bell, TELUS, SaskTel and TbayTel is an estimate by province population, not a licence-by-licence computation.
AWS-4 (2000–2020/2180–2200) and WCS 2300: licensees identified from ISED site data, amounts not compiled (status 'unknown').
2500 MHz: 2015 table used with 2006 Tier 3 populations; later residual sales (2018 H blocks) only partly applied; unassigned remainder ≈1–8 MHz.
ISED Spectrum Management System licence search (sms-sgs.ic.gc.ca) was unreachable; transfers after the auctions were checked only via the Sep 2026 site-data extract and operator reports.
Elite General Partnership (3800 MHz) affiliation not established.
